title: American beef stew
subtitle: Hearty American beef stew with potato and carrot
excerpt: Chunks of chuck beef braised with potato, carrot, onion, and celery in a thick, Worcestershire-spiked beef gravy. The American home-cooking standard, thicker and more vegetable-heavy than its European counterparts.
sourceNotes: American beef stew appears in Fannie Farmer's The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896, public domain) and in Joy of Cooking (1931). The thicker, potato-rich American version differs from French boeuf bourguignon and Irish stew in its use of Worcestershire sauce, tomato paste, and a flour-thickened gravy.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well. The potatoes can become slightly grainy on freezing; add them fresh when reheating if you prefer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Better the next day. Reheat gently with a splash of stock.

content.text: American beef stew is thicker and more substantial than most European equivalents. The flour coating on the beef, together with the potato starch released during cooking, turns the braising liquid into a proper, spoon-coating gravy. It is a one-pot meal that needs nothing alongside it except bread for the gravy.

items.prepNote: waxy, peeled, cut into chunks; add in the last 45 minutes

content.text: Season the beef with salt and pepper and toss in the flour to coat. Heat the oil in a large, heavy casserole over high heat. Brown the beef in batches, without crowding. 3 to 4 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Cook the onion, carrot, and celery for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the stock, add the Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay leaves. Stir to scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.

Return the beef to the pot. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a low simmer. Cover and cook on the hob for 1.5 hours, or in a 160°C oven. Add the potatoes in the last 45 minutes. Cook until the beef and potatoes are completely tender. Remove the bay leaves and thyme. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

items.cause: Flour coating was shaken off the beef, or not enough potato starch
items.fix: Mix 1 tablespoon of cornflour with 2 tablespoons cold water and stir into the stew. Simmer for 5 minutes to thicken.

content.text: American beef stew is the workhorse of American home cooking, the dish that appears in Joy of Cooking, Better Homes and Gardens, and every church cookbook in the country. It differs from boeuf bourguignon in that it does not use wine, from Irish stew in that it uses a thickened gravy rather than a clear broth, and from beef goulash in that it does not use paprika. It is its own thing: American, direct, and enormously satisfying.
